prayerExcerpt.en-US: He can no longer have God for his Father, who has not the Church for his mother.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Já não pode ter a Deus por Pai quem não tem a Igreja por mãe.

meta.face: Cornelius: a man of about sixty with a long, rectangular face — a broad, flat forehead and a straight-edged jaw; a long, straight nose with a narrow ridge; large dark almond eyes set rather close under level grey brows; flat cheeks; a flat, square chin; a small, thin-lipped mouth; bald on the crown with a close fringe of grey hair, a short, neat grey beard and a calm, grave look. Cyprian: a man of about fifty with a warm olive-brown North African complexion and a diamond-shaped face — a narrow forehead, wide, angular, jutting cheekbones and a narrow chin; a strong, high-bridged nose with flared nostrils; large, round dark eyes under thick, low, straight black brows; a full, wide mouth; thick, tightly curled black hair, a full black beard parted into two points at the chin, and an expression both grave and serene.
meta.basis: Cornelius follows the 12th-century apse mosaic of Santa Maria in Trastevere (balding, grey-haired, short grey beard, pallium) and the horn attribute from his name. Cyprian follows Dionysius's hierarch entry (young, curly hair, a large beard parted in two) and Pontius's note that his countenance was grave and joyous; the olive complexion is a choice for a Carthaginian, not attested.
meta.excerpt: Cyprian, On the Unity of the Church 6, ANF vol. 5 (1886), https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/050701.htm; pt-BR our rendering
